title: U.S. stocks fall as Nvidia’s Huang resigns and oil prices surge
text:
U.S. stocks fall as Nvidia’s Huang resigns and oil prices surge - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 13일(금) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English International U.S. stocks fall as Nvidia's Huang resigns and oil prices surge 
 입력 2026.11.13. 07:19 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 All three major U.S. stock indexes fell on the 12th (local time). The market was hit by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and a sharp rise in oil prices.
 Traders work on the floor of the NYSE. /Courtesy of Reuters On the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 52,297.09, down 189.40 points, or 0.36%. The S&P 500 fell 26.98 points, or 0.35%, to 7,592.40, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 101.10 points, or 0.39%, to 25,366.09.
 Nvidia fell 4.34% to close at $166.19. The intraday drop approached 12%, but bargain hunting narrowed the loss. After CEO Huang abruptly resigned, Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. The stock slid as the founder's departure increased management uncertainty.
 Rivals AMD and Broadcom jumped 5.78% and 5.87%, respectively. Investors bet that Nvidia's leadership gap could give competitors a chance to gain market share.
 Rising crude prices also weighed on stocks. U.S. President Donald Trump said there was no need to make a deal with Iran, heightening concerns about supply disruptions. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 2.55% on the day, and Brent crude gained 3.30%. On expectations that higher oil could stoke inflation, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose 13 basis points (1 bp = 0.01 percentage point) to 5.12%.
 With October's U.S. consumer price index (CPI) topping market expectations and oil rising, the odds of additional interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed) increased.
